text: For shared-model/data/budget optimizer comparisons BELOW task-specific saturation, use cumulative displacement Δ as a progress proxy, not a universal test-loss ranking. Check K1004/K1071-K1073 before choosing maximum Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T; Adagrad: 2·lr·√T; SGD: lr·T·|g|/(1-m), |g|≈0.01 (bigram 0.003; momentum MSE 0.03, K1019). Older backtests favored larger Δ in ~85% after ceiling exceptions, but not every 256-2048-step task is under-trained. Across different architectures or optimizers, close Δ estimates are not decisive (K1012); use scoped architecture rules. Long-budget spiral/XOR maxima can lose (q_fb4a7f/q_46d72e); no validated general ceiling yet.
mechanism: Displacement estimates optimization progress before saturation; test loss can instead be limited by stability, fine fitting or generalization after sufficient progress. These phases differ by task/model/budget.
phase: progress-limited training; conditional on not being in an evidenced saturation regime

text: Adagrad vs Adam/AdamW on the SAME architecture/budget: Adagrad Δ≈2·lr·√T, so comparable progress needs lr≈√T/2 (8-23×) higher. At lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam≤3, Adam-family wins65/70; ratio10 is mixed4/7; ratio≥30 Adagrad wins9/9. For shared-architecture Adagrad rate comparisons, larger lr usually wins (original40/41; broader univariate lab73/78, history13/16), not always; lr3e-3 is not a universal safety guarantee. Do not use this rate preference to settle LN/activation changes (q_cd8a07). At lr≤1e-4, Δ≤0.01 over T≤2048 indicates little progress relative to adaptive rates≥3e-5, but freezing is approximate.

SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.

LR/Δ exceptions: do NOT assume maximum Δ or lr3e-3 is always safe. MSE RMSprop lr≥1e-3: versus ≥3× smaller Δ, wins22/36 corpus (better MLP6/6, equal12/22, worse4/8); at equal lr prefer Adam (RMSprop3e-3 loses33/35). Univariate lower-RMSprop-rate preference can occur even below this ceiling (K1063). Bigram optima depend on model width (K1071); wide multilayer univariate high-Δ fitting risk is comparative, not automatic last place (K1072). Tabular optimum changes with epochs/data rule (K1073). Short-budget XOR/spiral often benefit from high rates, but T2048 winners q_46d72e/q_fb4a7f refute blanket long-budget safety; no general replacement ceiling is validated.
mechanism: RMSprop's first steps are lr/sqrt(small square-avg) ≈ up to 10× lr with no momentum smoothing; in unnormalized MLPs these kicks inflate hidden activations and the MSE output, so training oscillates. LayerNorm bounds hidden scale (and residual paths keep the function near-identity), absorbing the kicks — predicts instability only when the RMSprop net lacks LN/residual, as observed (6/6 vs 4/8).

text: MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).
mechanism: SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so each un-normalized block halves signal and gradient; stacked smooth blocks attenuate more under small-step optimizers (SGD ratio ~2-5 vs Adam ~1.1, Adam rescales gradients). LN restores scale, which is why an extra LN outweighs the activation (17/33). Predicts the penalty grows with depth and with SGD, and vanishes with per-layer normalisation of every block.

text: Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). text: LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.
mechanism: A pre-LN right before the last hidden Linear restores unit feature scale feeding the head, so tiny updates (Δ<0.1) move the output more; each unnormalized block after it shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU). Predicts the advantage fades once Δ≥0.1 (feature scale is learned) - observed 3/6. Why univariate/XOR don't follow is unexplained.

text: Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).
mechanism: Depth adds composed nonlinear capacity that, with only 1024 rows and 12+ noise coordinates, is spent fitting distractor structure once the data has been revisited many times; the overfit cost scales with epochs, not with Δ alone. So the Δ at which shallow-wide nets overtake deep ones falls as epochs rise (4→32). Predicts: at ≤4 epochs the K1009 Δ≥0.1 threshold holds; at Δ<0.03 nets are still boundary-limited and depth/LN help.

text: SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).
mechanism: SiLU'(0)=0.5, so each block halves small-signal gradients; LN fixes forward scale but not this derivative attenuation. SGD has no per-parameter rescaling, so the attenuation directly shrinks effective step size, compounding with depth; Adam's 1/√v undoes it. Predicts: effect grows with SiLU depth (5>4 blocks), vanishes under Adam-family, and cannot overcome a large normalization deficit where LN itself is needed (≥2 LN gap on oscillatory sums).

text: Classification MLPs (tabular, XOR, spiral), NON-residual, depth≥2, all choices on the same SGD (plain or momentum): the net whose LAST hidden block has LayerNorm wins 31/31 lab within-set pairs (14 sets, median CE ratio 0.69) - even when it has FEWER LayerNorms in total (11/11, ratio 0.76). An unnormalized tail undoes earlier LN (q_1af0fa: a deep net with internal LN but 2 unnormalized final blocks lost to a shallower wider net; normalizing those blocks cut CE 0.69→0.47 in a controlled rerun). With adaptive optimizers the edge is weaker: Adam 70/102 (ratio 0.92), Adagrad 21/35 (~0.99). Regression: univariate 17/25, multivariate 20/35 - not reliable.
mechanism: Under small SGD steps, update size scales with gradient magnitude; unnormalized ReLU/SiLU blocks after the last LN contract activations and backpropagated gradients, so the head and late layers barely move. Adaptive optimizers rescale per-parameter steps and largely cancel this attenuation, which predicts the much weaker edge under Adam/Adagrad (observed 0.92-0.99 ratios).

text: CLASSIFICATION MLPs (XOR/spiral/tabular), shared optimizer, Δ<0.1: RESIDUAL net vs NON-residual depth≥4 net with MORE LayerNorms — look at the plain net's LAST hidden block. Last block un-normalized → the residual net wins (lab SGD 16/16, CE ratio 0.72; adaptive 5/9; corpus 5/5): LNs followed by an unnormalized tail don't count. Last block LN'd → family-dependent: XOR+SGD plain wins 9/10; spiral+Adam-family plain wins 22/23 (residual CE ×1.3-1.4); spiral+SGD residual wins (lab 3/3, controlled 2/2, ratio 0.3-0.8); tabular ~coin flip (lab 12/27, corpus 6/6 plain). Moving LN to the last block (same count) lowered plain CE in 6/6 controlled cells.
mechanism: An unnormalized final block after LN'd blocks re-shrinks/attenuates features right before the head, so the plain net's earlier LNs buy little; a residual path carries signal past it. Predicts: the effect vanishes once the plain tail is LN'd (observed), and weakens at larger Δ where every net trains (observed at Δ≥0.1).

text: UNIVARIATE regression, RMSprop vs RMSprop (same MLP, different lr): the LOWER RMSprop lr usually wins, even at small Δ — lab larger-lr wins 9/42 (10 experiment groups; T=256 width≥128: 3/24, median MSE ratio 3.6; lr 1e-4 vs 3e-5: 3/11), corpus 2/3. At T=1024 on narrow nets it is a coin flip (4/9). RMSprop as the larger-Δ choice against Adam/AdamW of the same net also loses (lab 0/21 at RMSprop lr≥3e-4). Do not apply max-Δ to RMSprop on univariate MSE; multivariate is a coin flip (11/25).
mechanism: PyTorch RMSprop has no bias correction and a zero-init square average (alpha 0.99), so early steps are ~lr/sqrt(1-0.99^t) ≈ up to 10× lr, kicking a 1-D smooth fit off its low-MSE basin; the transient matters most at short T, predicting the effect fades at T=1024 (observed: 4/9).

text: BIGRAM LM learning-rate sweet spot (same model; choices differ in optimizer/lr/T; Δ per K1001): past a model-specific optimum MORE Δ LOSES - the solver's most common LM miss. d32/d64 transformers and GRUs: optimum Δ≈0.1-0.3 (Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024, 1e-3 at T=256; Adagrad 3e-3); ≥2× more Δ than a rival already at 0.1-0.3 loses (lab transformer 1/44, GRU 1/6, CE +2-20%); Δ≥1 loses to any rival with Δ≥0.03 (lab 0/17; q_c3a179). d_model=128 post-LN transformer: optimum ≈0.03-0.1; larger loses 0/11 once rival Δ≥0.03 (q_88802d AdamW 3e-3×256 last). Below the optimum max-Δ holds (13/13; GRU 14/15). Corpus: pick 'Δ nearest 0.2 (0.1 for d128)' 52/65 vs max-Δ 43/65.
mechanism: Labels are sampled from P(y|x), so minibatch gradients carry irreducible noise; with a constant lr, once the V×V table is fit further displacement only adds noise-driven parameter jitter and memorisation of the 800 training windows (positions/contexts), raising test CE. More parameters per token (d_model 128) reach that fit point at smaller Δ, so the optimum shifts down with width - predicting d128 < d64 ≈ d32 optimum, as observed.

mechanism: Both nets must learn a current-token lookup. When nearly frozen, the GRU's gates pass the input embedding straight to the output, so tiny updates already cut CE, while the transformer must first beat random positional embeddings and attention mixing. Once Δ≥0.02 the transformer's residual stream carries token identity and its FF fits the table faster than a 2-layer non-residual GRU; by Δ≥0.1 post-LN transformers overshoot (K1071), returning the edge to the GRU.
